Seminar Title:

Slice-Level Fault Mitigation in SRAM-Based FPGAs Using Dynamic Reconfiguration.

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

prof. Atin Mukherjee

Speaker Type:

Faculty

Venue:

SoC Design Laboratory (EC-230), NIT Rourkela

Date and Time:

12 Nov 2026 3.00PM

Contact:

Prof. Atin Mukherjee

Abstract:

SRAM-based field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) are popular in safety-critical and radiation-prone appli cations due to their high performance and reconfigurability. However, these devices are susceptible to radiation induced soft errors and single event upsets (SEUs) that can affect the configuration memory and reduces the system reliability. In this paper, we propose an area-efficient fault-tolerant FPGA architecture implemented at the slice level on the Xilinx Virtex-E FPGA platform. The proposed work studies and compares several fault tolerant techniques such as triple modular redundancy (TMR), master-slave based TMR and dynamic reconfiguration. We propose a dynamic reconfigurable slice architecture with built-in self-test (BIST) mechanism, spare look up table (LUT) and multiplexer based runtime recovery to detect and mitigate the LUT faults without stopping the FPGA operation in normal mode. Furthermore, automated Xilinx design constraint (XDC) generation with TCL scripting is used to prevent logic placement on faulty FPGA slices. Simulation analysis and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed dynamic reconfiguration technique achieves better performance quality metric (PQM) with much lower area overhead than the traditional TMR and other popular architectures. The proposed architecture offers an effective trade-off between reliability, hardware utilization and fault recovery for reliable FPGA-based systems.
